investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would populate those fields.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which submits the pod that cannot be scheduled, so the probe times out without ever writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState into the evidence object.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no VM slots remain for new remote agent pods, and preemption found no evictable victims

Secondary: node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 qualify for kata.peerpods.io/vm), so even if other nodes had capacity they would not be used

Tertiary: a prior stuck or leaked remote agent pod (consistent with the recent commit message '574b6b2 fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents') may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, preventing new allocations
Lower confidence: the cluster may have been scaled down or a node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing available VM slots below demand

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval never reached the state-polling phase, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod (2 nodes have the required resource but it is fully consumed; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector). Because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~136–146 seconds across all three checks, createAgent() in the eval runner never returned a live agent, and the state-polling step was never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary: The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes have no remaining vm slots and no preemptible victims, making preemption also impossible.

Tertiary: A concurrent surge of remote agent workloads (from real users or other eval runs) may have saturated the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, causing a transient capacity exhaustion rather than a permanent shortage.

Lower confidence: The node pool for kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been scaled down or a node may have become NotReady, reducing available capacity from a previously sufficient level. No node health data is present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and unused on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling error would have a different root cause (e.g., a node selector misconfiguration or a Kubernetes scheduler bug).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner never reached the agent-creation logic that would populate those fields.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which submits the pod that cannot be scheduled, so the probe times out without ever writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState into the evidence object.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 136s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 146s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 143s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the runner never progressed past pod scheduling
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with a pre-agent-creation failure

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — this is the call that submits the pod; failure here prevents any downstream evidence writes
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141122 (~136s active wait) matches the scheduler's reported stuck duration of 136s, confirming the probe hit its timeout waiting for the pod
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no VM slots remain for new remote agent pods, and preemption found no evictable victims

Secondary: node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 qualify for kata.peerpods.io/vm), so even if other nodes had capacity they would not be used

Tertiary: a prior stuck or leaked remote agent pod (consistent with the recent commit message '574b6b2 fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents') may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, preventing new allocations
Lower confidence: the cluster may have been scaled down or a node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing available VM slots below demand

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval never reached the state-polling phase, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval pod (2 nodes have the required resource but it is fully consumed; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector). Because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~136–146 seconds across all three checks, createAgent() in the eval runner never returned a live agent, and the state-polling step was never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): contract requires ['orgId','agentId','readyState','state'] — none were produced.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary: The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes have no remaining vm slots and no preemptible victims, making preemption also impossible.

Tertiary: A concurrent surge of remote agent workloads (from real users or other eval runs) may have saturated the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, causing a transient capacity exhaustion rather than a permanent shortage.

Lower confidence: The node pool for kata.peerpods.io/vm may have been scaled down or a node may have become NotReady, reducing available capacity from a previously sufficient level. No node health data is present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm node resource — cluster infrastructure
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes extended resource kata.peerpods.io/vm is exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the remote agent pod's affinity selector. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain (failed-check.message).

recommendedNextActions: Check the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that match the remote agent pod's affinity selector and compare against current allocations to determine whether this is a capacity shortage or a slot leak.
If stuck pods are found holding VM slots, terminate them to free capacity and re-run the eval probes to confirm recovery.

If VM slot capacity is genuinely insufficient for concurrent eval probe runs plus any production workload, consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes or adding additional affinity-eligible nodes to the cluster.

Review whether the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods is intentionally restricting scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and assess whether additional nodes should be made eligible to increase the schedulable pool.

Monitor the next scheduled eval run after any remediation to confirm all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return to passing status with full evidence output.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling failure is still active. A pass would indicate transient exhaustion; a repeat fail with the same message confirms sustained capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three failing remote-agents checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks share the same scheduling root cause and that none have recovered independently.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect pending and running pods with the remote agent node selector in the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether stuck or leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, which is the leading hypothesis for why capacity is exhausted.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-matching nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures whether the VM resource slots are genuinely exhausted or whether the scheduling failure has a different cause such as a misconfigured resource request.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run local-agent-create and local-agent-runtime checks to confirm failure is isolated to remote agents
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Local agent checks do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm. If they pass, the failure is confirmed to be scoped to the remote agent VM scheduling layer and not a broader API or auth outage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure produces a passing result with all 5 evidence fields present, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a competing pod completed and freed a slot) rather than a sustained capacity deficit.

If kubectl or cluster tooling shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes is non-zero and no pods are currently consuming it, the scheduling failure may have a different cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request on the eval pod itself).

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to actually be eligible (i.e., the affinity selector was recently changed and is now too restrictive), the root cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If no stuck or leaked remote agent pods are found on the cluster, the hypothesis that prior eval runs are holding VM slots would be disproved, pointing instead to genuine capacity shortage or a scale-down event.
If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks are also failing at the same time, the failure scope may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm layer alone.
followUpEvals: Add an eval check that directly probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1 free slot), so capacity exhaustion is detected before pod scheduling fails.

Add an eval check that detects and reports remote agent pods stuck in Pending or Terminating state for longer than a configurable threshold, providing early warning of slot leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms all remote agent pods created during an eval run are fully terminated within a bounded time window, catching cases where the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs fails to release VM slots.

Consider adding a pre-flight eval step that checks for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and skips or warns rather than timing out after 136–151 s when capacity is known to be zero.
